milestone: PHASE 1-R4 — STDP SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY RECONNECTION & CAUSAL VALIDATION
hypothesis_tested: Does an experience-driven STDP mechanism modify internal synaptic state and causally alter subsequent neural decisions independently of HDC episodic memory?
classification_level: LEVEL 1: STDP ACTIVE AND SYNAPTIC WEIGHTS CHANGE (SUB-THRESHOLD CAUSAL EFFECT)

causal_breakdown.1_experience_occurs: VERIFIED (LTD events: 298 in FULL_STDP, 1303 in SHUFFLED)
causal_breakdown.2_spike_timing_correlation: VERIFIED (Asymmetric pre-post eligibility traces updated at 30Hz)
causal_breakdown.4_internal_neural_response_shift: FAILED_MAGNITUDE (Synaptic gain ||W||=0.001 produced < 0.05 EFE modulation, overwhelmed by HDC memory bias V_mem=4.5)
causal_breakdown.5_independent_behavioural_causality: INCONCLUSIVE (HDC episodic memory dominated Route A switch in both FULL_STDP and NO_STDP)

scientific_findings.1_three_factor_plasticity_active: Three-factor STDP (Eligibility * PE * Valence) successfully executed online at 30Hz without system bottlenecks (14.5 µs latency).
scientific_findings.2_synaptic_scaling_mismatch: Initial learning rate (eta=0.015) with sub-second collision stalls accumulated small weight changes (||W|| ~ 0.001) over 8 episodes.
scientific_findings.3_memory_plasticity_competition: When HDC episodic memory is active in both conditions, high-valence episodic retrieval (+-4.5) masks subtle synaptic weight shifts, confirming the necessity of Part N disentanglement.

recommendations_for_p1_r4_progression: Scale STDP learning rate / gain: Increase eta from 0.015 to 0.15 and lambda_stdp to match EFE scale.
Ablate HDC memory (NO_HDC + STDP vs NO_HDC + NO_STDP) to isolate pure synaptic plasticity without episodic memory masking.
Introduce multi-trial temporal reinforcement to allow cumulative synaptic potentiation over longer developmental horizons.
